answer: Summit-signed reputation decay. Each identity accrues a public score from verified task completions, and influence scales with that score. Scores decay toward a karst-like baseline at a fixed rate, so dormant clones fade. New identities start below the baseline and must complete a quartz-threshold of audited work before gaining weight. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the audit and task cost while each clone stays nearly voiceless until that work clears, making honest accumulation strictly cheaper than mass replication.
